proposal.rationale: The asset currently runs the classical tls13-x25519 profile, which is below the required security floor (hybrid-pqc). Of the allowlisted PQC-capable profiles, tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 (implementation liboqs-0.16.0, present on the asset) has the most ready peers: peer-01 and peer-03 both have readiness 'known' and advertise the required 'kem:x25519mlkem768' capability. peer-02 lacks that capability (only advertises 'kem:x25519') and is therefore not eligible for this migration. peer-04 also advertises the required capability and would technically be ready, but per the engineering notes it is scheduled for decommissioning next week and has been intentionally left out of this batch. The competing pqc-class profile tls13-mlkem768 has zero ready peers (none advertise 'kem:mlkem768'), so despite its higher security class it does not achieve the maximum ready-endpoint count and is not selected. No peer readiness is unresolved \u2014 all listed peers report readiness 'known'; peer-02 and peer-04 are excluded for capability and decommission reasons respectively, not readiness uncertainty. Recommend executing within the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window with the on-call network team as rollback owner, and monitoring handshake error rates for 30 minutes post-change per the change window note.
